Plan PIM deployment
Planning a PIM deployment is a critical step for organizations aiming to enhance their security
posture and idx_986e0984 manage access to sensitive resources effectively. Without thorough planning,
organizations may face challenges in assigning the correct roles, ensuring compliance, and
maintaining visibility over privileged activities. A well-conceived deployment plan helps
identify which roles require PIM, ensures that all licensing requirements are met, and
establishes clear processes for approval and activation workflows. This preparation not only
minimizes the risk of unauthorized access but also streamlines the user experience for those
who legitimately need elevated privileges.
Furthermore, planning allows organizations to align PIM implementation with broader IT
governance and compliance objectives. By mapping out business needs, regulatory
requirements, and operational processes beforehand, organizations can configure PIM settings
—such as approval requirements, notification policies, and auditing mechanisms—in a way
that supports both security and productivity. It also provides an opportunity to educate
stakeholders about the new processes, reducing confusion and resistance during rollout. A
strategic approach to PIM deployment ensures that privileged access is granted only when
necessary, for the right duration, and under proper oversight, thereby reducing the attack
surface and supporting ongoing risk management efforts.
It is recommended idx_8d2e57bb to start with a pilot which will consist of a small set of test users to ensure
that PIM behaves as expected. Develop test cases to test all aspects of PIM, like PIM for Entra
roles, Azure roles, and groups. This should include members of a group, members of a role, IT
service owner, subscription or resource owner in Azure and owners of groups. This way you
can verify that all configuration is set up correctly and move to production with confidence.
Communication is critical for the success of PIM. Proactively communicate with users and
educate them on how their experience will change and how they can get support if required. It
is also important to have a rollback plan in place in case PIM fails to work as desired.
269 Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
Microsoft Entra and Azure roles
Before idx_ece5d539 starting implementation, it is important to plan. The idx_e8114a2f following steps will assist you in
preparing to manage idx_757e48ed Microsoft Entra idx_3493c4dc and Azure roles using PIM:

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 8 268
chunks.content:
Discover privileged roles: List users that have privileged roles in the tenant. Review
their access, identify users who don't need that access and remove it if required. You
can use Microsoft Entra access reviews to automate this process.
Identify the roles to be managed by PIM: Prioritize the roles that have the most
permissions to be managed by PIM first. Ensure that Global Administrator and Security
Administrator are PIM managed as those are highly privileged and can cause the most
harm if compromised. Next, consider the roles that may be most susceptible to attack.
Microsoft Entra identifies privileged roles with a PRIVILEGED label. Use that to identify
other privileged roles.
For Azure, it is recommended that all Subscription Owner and User Access
Administrator roles be managed using PIM.
Configure settings: Identify the settings you would like to configure for the identified
roles. For example, you might want all requests for the Global Administrator idx_e8792ebe role to be
manually approved, and the idx_8d4b0adc role be activated for only one hour.
Once this groundwork is done you can proceed with creating role assignments for eligible
users.
Groups
Sometimes users idx_2c8a38ab could have multiple eligible assignments in Microsoft Entra. They would
have to activate each role individually. To make matters worse, they may have multiple Azure
resources assigned to them for which they need to elevate permissions using PIM. This is
where PIM for Groups helps. PIM for Groups can be used to govern access to resources like
Microsoft Entra roles, Azure roles, Azure SQL, Azure Key Vault, Intune and other applications. It
is important to identify the groups that you would like to manage using PIM. Any cloud-only
Microsoft 365 or Security group with static membership can be enabled for PIM for Groups.
Using nested groups is not recommended. These groups are assigned permanent active access
to resources, and their membership or ownership is then managed using PIM. Both role-
assignable groups and non-role-assignable groups can be enabled for PIM for Groups. If you

want to assign Microsoft Entra roles to a group, a role-assignable group must be created. Role-
assignable groups is explained in Chapter 2, Fundamentals of Microsoft Entra ID.
It is recommended to create a role-assignable group even if you don't intend to assign roles to
the group, but the group provides access to sensitive resources. This is because role-assignable
groups have extra protection built in, such as:
Only Global Administrators, Privileged Role Administrators, or the group owner can
manage a role-assignable group.
No other user can change the credentials of members of a role-assignable group. This
prevents an administrator from elevating to a higher privileged role without going
through an approval process.
Microsoft Entra ID does not allow removal of the last active owner of a group. For example, if a
group has an active owner user A and an eligible owner user B, user B activates their ownership
of the group using PIM. Meanwhile, user A is removed from group ownership or from the
idx_bdd27477 tenant. In this case, the deactivation of the owner role for user B will not succeed as they are
the last active owner. PIM will try to deactivate the owner role for user B for 30 days and if
another owner is not added within 30 days, PIM will stop attempting the deactivation and
user B will continue as the owner of the group.
Start using PIM
With all the idx_d8654f09 basics covered, you are now ready to start using PIM. You can now create eligible
or time-bound assignments for Microsoft Entra and Azure roles. The following sections explain
the PIM process for Microsoft Entra roles, Azure roles, and groups.
Microsoft Entra roles
By enabling PIM for Entra roles, organizations can move from standing admin access to just-
in-time, time-bound elevation, dramatically reducing the attack surface. Using PIM for Entra
roles, administrators idx_87820364 can request elevated permissions when they need to carry out a
privileged task, such as password resets or idx_8a169d25 creating Conditional Access policies. This access can
be time-bound and automatically revoked after a predetermined time. By eliminating
unnecessary permanent assignments and adding oversight to high-impact roles, PIM helps
organizations prevent misuse, contain credential compromise, and maintain a clean, least-
privileged environment that aligns with zero-trust principles.
Enabling PIM for Microsoft Entra roles has a few steps. These are detailed below.

prepared for PIM. A Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator is required to edit

Auditing PIM
The Resource audit section of PIM shows all assignments and activations for Microsoft Entra
roles, Azure idx_aff75aa5 resource roles, and Groups for the past 30 days. To retain audit data for longer than
30 days you can use Azure Monitor to send it to an Azure storage account. To access the
Resource audit section, navigate to ID Governance | Privileged Identity Management and
select Microsoft Entra roles, Azure resources or Groups. Then select Resource audit. The

Best practices
Here are idx_417910c6 the best practices for deploying Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in Microsoft
Entra, written to be crisp, actionable, and aligned with strong governance principles.
Best practices for PIM
The following are some best practices that help organizations get the most value out of PIM:
Enforce Just-in-Time access: Convert all standing privileged assignments into eligible
roles. This reduces the attack surface and aligns with Zero-Trust by ensuring admin
rights exist only when needed.
Require MFA for activation: Make MFA mandatory for every privileged activation.
This blocks compromised credentials from being used to elevate access.
Use approval workflows for high-impact roles: Roles such as Global Administrator,
Privileged Role Administrator, and User Administrator should require explicit approval
before activation.
•
•
•
297 Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management
Set short activation durations: Keep activation windows minimal, just long enough
to complete the task. Shorter windows reduce exposure and limit misuse.
Require justification for every activation: Require business justification for each
elevation. This strengthens auditability and supports compliance reviews.
Enable alerts for suspicious or excessive activations: Monitor unusual patterns such
as idx_c356f5d0 repeated activations, after-hours use, or unexpected role requests.
Use access reviews regularly: Schedule periodic reviews for eligible role assignments,
active assignments, and PIM-enabled groups. This keeps privileged access clean and
current.
Prefer PIM for groups for shared access: When multiple users need the same
privileged role, manage it through PIM for Groups to simplify lifecycle management
and reduce admin overhead.
Integrate PIM with Conditional Access: Use Conditional Access to enforce compliant
devices, trusted locations, and risk-based controls. This adds layered protection to
privileged activations.
Audit and log everything: Ensure all PIM activities feed into Microsoft Entra audit
logs. Consider sending alerts to a SIEM such as Microsoft Sentinel. Visibility is essential
for governance and incident response.
Avoid permanent assignments except for break-glass accounts: Keep only two
emergency accounts with permanent Global Administrator rights, protected by long,
complex passwords and strict monitoring.
Communicate and train admins: Ensure admins understand how to activate roles
and why PIM is required.

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 8 296
chunks.content:
These best practices ensure that organizations adequately protect the accounts that hold the
keys to the kingdom.
Summary
This chapter started with explaining the concept of privileged identities and went on to
explain how Microsoft Entra PIM manages privileged identities. It explained the terminology
used in PIM, how roles are assigned and the licensing requirements. This chapter taught you
how you can plan PIM deployment for Microsoft Entra and Azure roles and Groups. It then
explained the detailed steps in configuring and managing PIM for Microsoft Entra roles, Azure
roles, and Groups. It ended with introducing alerts and auditing. It also covered how
organizations starting their PIM journey can utilize the discovery and insights feature. In the
next chapter, we will learn how to protect user identities using Microsoft Entra ID Protection.

Part 3 focuses on strengthening trust across every identity that interacts with your
environment: human, device, and workload. It begins with Microsoft Entra ID Protection,
which provides continuous risk detection and adaptive safeguards to defend against
compromised identities. This section then explores Microsoft Entra Verified ID, enabling
decentralized, verifiable credentials that enhance privacy and assurance. Finally, it examines
Workload ID, the identity foundation for applications, services, and automation. Together,
these chapters illustrate how Microsoft Entra builds a resilient trust fabric that protects access,
validates authenticity, and secures the expanding digital ecosystem.

9
Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Identity protection is a critical component of modern cybersecurity strategies, particularly as
organizations increasingly adopt cloud-based and hybrid environments. The goal of identity
protection is to safeguard digital identities from unauthorized access, misuse, or compromise.
This involves a combination of proactive measures, continuous monitoring, and responsive
actions to detect and address potential threats.
One of the idx_3cde3801 fundamental aspects of identity protection is implementing robust authentication
mechanisms. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is commonly used to add an additional
layer of security, ensuring that even if a password is compromised, unauthorized users are less
likely to gain access. Alongside MFA, policies such as conditional access help organizations
control who can access resources, under what circumstances, and from which locations or
devices.
Advanced identity idx_087e1d55 protection solutions, like Microsoft Entra ID Protection, go further by
leveraging machine learning and behavioral analytics to detect suspicious activities in real
time. These systems can identify anomalies such as impossible travel, unusual sign-in
patterns, or atypical device usage. When a risk is detected, automated responses can be
triggered, such as prompting for additional verification, blocking access, or alerting security
teams. By integrating with SIEM tools, identity protection systems also support broader threat
detection and incident response efforts, contributing to a holistic security posture.
This chapter will cover:
Risk conditions
Risk-based Conditional Access
Investigating and remediating risks
•
•
•
Introduction to Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Microsoft Entra ID Protection helps organizations detect, investigate, and remediate
identity-based risks. It helps idx_5f444bcf safeguard user identities by detecting risky sign-ins and accounts
using signals collected from a vast global ecosystem. These signals come from trillions of
Microsoft services and devices—such as Microsoft Accounts, Xbox, Windows, and Azure—
which provide data on user behavior, device health, and sign-in patterns. Microsoft also
collaborates with security researchers and law enforcement to track known threats like
malicious IPs and hacker tools. Additionally, feedback from users and administrators helps
refine the system's accuracy. All these inputs are processed by Microsoft's risk evaluation
engine, which uses machine learning to identify suspicious activities like impossible travel,
password spray attacks, or anonymous browser usage. Based on these detections, Entra ID
Protection can automatically trigger security responses, such as requiring multi-factor
authentication or blocking access.

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 11, Microsoft Entra Workload ID
chunks.content:
The following picture explains Microsoft Entra ID Protection:
Figure 9.1: Microsoft Entra ID protection
Any identified risks are tracked and reported in reports such as Risk detections, Risky users,
and Risky sign-ins which administrators can use to investigate and remediate risks.
From an attacker's point of view, the biggest obstacle today isn't stealing passwords. It is
getting past MFA. Modern idx_a952a128 adversaries increasingly use Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM)
phishing kits, which sit between the user and the legitimate sign-in page. These kits don't

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 304
chunks.content:
Chapter 9 304
break MFA; instead, they trick the user into completing MFA on a fake page, then quietly
capture the resulting session token.
To the attacker, this token is gold. It lets them impersonate the user without needing the
password or MFA again, because the session is already authenticated. This is why attackers
focus on session hijacking: it bypasses the very controls designed to stop them.
But this is also exactly where Identity Protection pushes back. Anomalous Token catches
tokens being used in ways that don't match how or where they were issued. AiTM detections
identify when a idx_aa71ce7b sign-in is routed through malicious infrastructure commonly used by phishing
kits.
From the attacker's perspective, this breaks the entire playbook: even if they manage to steal a
token, they can't rely on it lasting. The moment risk is detected, the session collapses.
Automation is the idx_0fb32e3d key to protecting the organization against risks. Risk-based Conditional
Access policies can be used to automatically remediate risky sign-ins and risky user
detections. Based on the risk level, a phishing-resistant MFA method or password reset could
be required. If the user can complete this, the risk is automatically remediated. If automation is
not enabled, an administrator will have to manually investigate and remediate risks.
Data from ID Protection can be sent to other tools for archival or further correlation and
investigation. ID Protection can idx_7a259d75 seamlessly integrate with Microsoft Sentinel, where signals
can be correlated with other Microsoft and non-Microsoft security products. Organizations
that want to retain data for longer can choose to send the data to a Log Analytics workspace, an
Azure storage account or Azure Event Hub.

Chapter 9 308
In Microsoft Entra ID Protection, an attack is an event where a bad actor is attempting to sign
in to a tenant. These attacks are detected by Microsoft's advanced risk detections and trigger a
real-time risk detection that is mapped to a MITRE ATT&CK technique. This is depicted by the
Attacks in your tenant graphic in Figure 9.2. This graphic shows attacks that impacted the
tenant over the last 30 days and if they were blocked during sign-in. The left side shows the
volume of each attack type during sign-in, and the right side shows the number of attacks
blocked or not remediated.
An attack is considered Blocked if the risky sign-in is interrupted by a Conditional
Access policy and the attacker is unsuccessful.
An attack is considered Not remediated if risky sign-ins were not interrupted and need
human intervention to be remediated. These risky sign-ins are available in the Risky
sign-ins report.
This graphic updates every 24 hour and shows the real-time sign risks.
To view the attack details, you can either click on the count of attacks on the left side of the
graphic or use the Risk detections page.
In addition to the above, the dashboard also provides a handy graph that displays the location
of the risky sign-ins for the tenant. The size of the red circle depicts the volume of attacks from
that location. Hovering over the red circle shows more details like the country name and the
number of risky sign-ins detected from that place.
Microsoft Entra idx_4630b8a4 ID Protection also shows recommendations based on the attacks detected in
the tenant over the last 30 days. This assists the administrators in taking quick actions to
improve their identity security posture.
Lastly, a recent activity summary is also displayed which shows the recent risk-related activity
in the tenant.
Understanding risk detections
Microsoft Entra ID Protection provides a continuous, intelligence-driven layer of defense by
detecting risky idx_e26a2512 user behavior, sign-ins, and credentials across your identity estate. At its core,
ID Protection uses signals from Microsoft's global threat intelligence spanning billions of daily
authentications, endpoint telemetry, and threat actor activity to identify anomalies that may
•
•
To learn idx_143bee8f more about MITRE ATT&CK refer to https://attack.mitre.org/.
Tip
309 Microsoft Entra ID Protection
indicate compromise. Microsoft Entra ID Protection provides a broad range of risk detections
that help identify suspicious activity in the tenant.
Risk types
Risk detections idx_8382f9e5 can be linked to a user or a sign-in event. Both user risk idx_6cf9ddc4 and sign-in risk
contribute to the user risk score found in the Risky user report.
User risk: A user risk is detected at the user level. These identify when a user account is

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 308
chunks.content:
at risk. For example, a bad actor may gain access to the account by compromising the
user's credentials or the user's credentials are found on the dark web. User risk is
cumulative and persists until remediated, making it a strong indicator for requiring
secure password reset or step-up verification. A user risk is cleared once a user
performs a secure password reset.
Sign-in risk: Sign-in risk is the possibility that the sign-in attempt is made by someone
other than the owner of the account. This highlights anomalies such as sign-ins from
anonymous browsers, suspicious token replay, and more. Sign-in risk is real-time and
transient, enabling conditional access policies to block or challenge risky attempts
immediately. Sign-in risk feeds user risk. A pattern of risky sign-ins (or a single high-
confidence one like leaked credentials) raises the user's risk level. One risky sign-in
usually won't flip a user to high risk but repeated or strong-signal sign-ins will. A sign-
in risk is cleared once a user successfully completes an MFA prompt.
It is important idx_bd6869b6 to understand that user risk reflects state and sign-in risk reflects idx_7703d6f2 events. Sign-
in risk is transient (about this login). User risk is cumulative (about the identity). Even if
today's sign-in looks clean, a user can still be flagged "high risk" because of past evidence.
Risk levels
Risk is categorized into three levels: low, medium, and high. Risk levels are calculated by
Microsoft's idx_164264ef machine learning algorithms and depict how confident Microsoft idx_bd0b3f53 is that a
particular user or sign-in is suspicious. Some detections can be categorized at all three levels
depending on the sign-in properties, while some may always be categorized as high, medium
or low. Risk levels play an important role in prioritizing, investigating, and remediating risk
detections. They also play an important role in configuring risk-based Conditional Access
policies. Each policy can be set to trigger at a particular risk level. The risk levels are explained
below.
High: Microsoft is highly confident that an account is compromised. Signals like threat
intelligence and known attack patterns are used to determine the confidence level of
risk detection.
•
•
•

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 9 310
chunks.content:
Chapter 9 310
Medium: One or more moderate severity anomalies are detected but there is less
confidence that the account is compromised.
Low: Anomalies may be present in the sign-in or user account but there is less
confidence that the account has been compromised.
Organizations can configure Conditional Access policies based on these risk levels. For
example, most organizations block access if the risk level is high, enforce MFA if it is medium
and allow access for low risk.
Detection types
Risks can idx_8f220530 be calculated in Real-time or Offline. This is designed to improve the precision of
user and sign-in risk detection.
Real-time risk detection: Detecting risks in real-time gives the opportunity to act
early and use risk-based Conditional Access policies to help users self-remediate and
prevent a bad actor from gaining access to the tenant. These risks show up in reporting
within 5-10 minutes.
Offline risk detections: These are calculated after authentication is complete. They
can provide more insight into how a bad actor gained access to the account. Offline
risks might show up in 48 hours.

Now that you understand the risk detections in detail, let's learn how we can use risk-based
access policies to mitigate these risks.
Risk-based access policies
Conditional idx_7c4417da Access policies can be applied to protect organizations when a sign-in or user risk
is detected. This is called risk-based Conditional Access (RBCA). The idx_4742c51d following graphic
explains how risk-based Conditional Access policies work to protect an organization's critical
resources.
Figure 9.3: Risk-based Conditional Access
In Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, there are two conditions for user-specific risk
conditions that are powered by Microsoft Entra ID Protection. These are Sign-in risk and User
risk. When administrators create these Conditional Access policies, they can configure these
conditions to take specific actions based on the identified risk level. During each sign-in,
Microsoft Entra ID Protection sends the detected risk level to Conditional Access. The policies
apply if the conditions are satisfied. For example, you might want a user to be prompted for
MFA only when idx_6998d551 the sign-in risk is medium or high. The main benefit of using RBCA is
automatic risk remediation. When a user successfully completes the required access control,
such as responding to MFA, their risk is remediated. No further action is needed from the
administrator. This reduces the burden of investigating and remediating the risk from the

Prerequisites
Before idx_08afb16c configuring risk-based Conditional Access policies, ensure that the following
prerequisites are met.
Ensure that the users are registered for MFA. Use the MFA registration policy explained
later in this section.
Ensure that idx_cd194389 users are registered for self-service password reset (SSPR). This has been
explained in Chapter 3, Implementing Microsoft Entra ID.
Configure emergency access accounts. This has been explained in Chapter 8, Microsoft
Entra Privileged Identity Management.
Configure named locations in Conditional Access. This should include your corporate
and VPN IP ranges. IP-based locations can be marked as trusted. Sign-ins from trusted
named locations lower sign-in risk and improve the accuracy of ID Protection risk
calculations.
Once all the prerequisites have been met, you can proceed with creating the sign-in risk and
user risk policies.
Sign-in risk policy
Microsoft idx_eb8bb11c Entra ID Protection analyzes idx_a8b1c505 hundreds of signals in real-time to calculate a sign-in
risk level for each sign-in. This risk level is sent to Conditional Access where administrators can
configure policies to enforce the following controls based on the risk level:
Block access
Allow access requiring MFA

configuring a Conditional Access policy.

Organizations idx_1b033d4c must choose the appropriate idx_6a3ba325 risk level to configure, balancing user experience
and security. Choosing to apply access policies to High risk level reduces the number of times a
policy is enforced. While this minimizes friction for users, it might not block all attacks.
Selecting Low risk level will increase the number of times users are interrupted. Microsoft
recommends requiring MFA for Medium and High sign-in risk levels. A successful MFA is the
only way to remediate a sign-in risk, regardless of the risk level.
User risk policy
Microsoft Entra ID Protection analyzes signals about user risk to calculate a risk level.
Behaviors idx_77c1f76d like risky sign-ins and credential leaks idx_45e753ec are used to calculate the user risk level. These
signals are then fed into Conditional Access where administrators can configure policies to
enforce the following controls based on the risk level:
Block access
If risks are detected, during sign-in, the user can take the action as enforced by the
policy to self-remediate. Users must be registered for Microsoft Entra MFA to enforce a
sign-in risk policy.

Chapter 9 320
To test a user risk policy, start with the policy in either Off or Report-only mode. Elevate the
risk level of a user by simulating one or more risk detections. Wait for some time to confirm if
the risk level is elevated. If not, simulate additional risk detections until the risk level is
elevated. Now turn the user risk policy On and sign in as the user with elevated risk level.
To test a sign-in risk policy, ensure that the policy is On. Now try to sign in using the Tor
browser.
The policies idx_7b68d2a1 should be triggered, and you idx_859cab53 should either be prompted to carry out the self-
remediation steps as defined in the policy or access should be blocked as per policy settings.
Impact analysis workbook
The deployment of risk-based Conditional Access policies requires careful planning, time, and
change idx_220c330a management. It is also critical to ensure that implementing these policies does not
cause disruptions to users and their ability to connect to resources to do their jobs.
Administrators must also be able to confidently convince the leadership that these policies will
not cause unwanted disruptions. One way to analyze the potential impact of these policies is to
create them in report-only mode and then wait for a few weeks or months to have the results.
This can delay the actual rollout of the policies, thereby exposing the organization to longer
risk periods and preventing you from enjoying the advantages. A quicker way of understanding
the potential impact is to use the Impact analysis of risk-based access policies workbook.
This workbook helps you understand your environment before enabling the policies that could
potentially block users from signing in, enforce MFA, or require a password reset. It provides
the following information for a time range of your choosing.
Impact summary of recommended risk-based policies including user risk, sign-in risk
and trusted network scenarios.
Impact details for user risk scenarios like high-risk user not blocked or prompted for
password change, users who performed a password change and remediated risk etc.
Impact details for sign-in risk scenarios like high-risk sign-ins not blocked or prompted
for MFA or high-risk sign-ins that completed MFA and self-remediated.
Network details like top IP addresses are not listed as trusted network locations.
This information can be used to identify which users will be impacted if risk-based Conditional
Access policies are implemented.
Using this workbook does not require creating risk-based Conditional Access policies
beforehand. However, you must have sign-in logs sent to a Log Analytics workspace in Azure.
For more information on how to do this, refer to https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/
entra/identity/monitoring-health/howto-use-workbooks.

Chapter 9 324
Continuous Access Evaluation
Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE) keeps access decisions alive instead of fixed at sign-in.
It lets apps idx_a8f3dce6 check back with Entra ID whenever something meaningful changes like risk,
location, or device posture so sessions stay aligned with real-time conditions. CAE turns
identity from a one-time check into an ongoing, adaptive trust signal. For example, a user signs
in to Outlook from their corporate network. Later, they walk next door and connect their
laptop to the café's public Wi-Fi. Without CAE, their Outlook session would continue because
Conditional Access was only evaluated at sign-in. With CAE, Entra detects the shift to an
untrusted network and signals Outlook to re-check the session immediately. Outlook forces re-
authentication, Conditional Access is re-evaluated, and access is either blocked or MFA-
challenged in near real-time without waiting for token expiry.
For CAE to work the client must be CAE-capable, the workload must support CAE and
Microsoft Entra ID must send real-time signals. SharePoint Online, Exchange Online, Teams,
and Microsoft Graph already support CAE and enforce real-time Conditional Access decisions.
Organizations can enable their applications for CAE by using CAE-aware authentication
libraries (like MSAL) and implement logic to handle CAE-specific error responses from the
resource API, prompting the app to re-authenticate when Entra ID signals that conditions have
changed.
CAE is auto enabled in all Microsoft Entra tenants. Organizations wishing to disable it can do
so using the session control in Conditional Access policies. Disabling CAE only works when
applied to all applications. It can, however, be applied to all users or selected users and groups.
Scenarios
CAE idx_016eba57 enables two key scenarios as described below:
Critical event evaluation
CAE is idx_44234632 achieved by allowing idx_d5369188 services such as Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and Teams
to subscribe to essential Microsoft Entra events. This approach facilitates the prompt
evaluation of these events and ensures that controls are enforced in near real time. Critical
events evaluated are:
User account deleted or disabled
User password changed
MFA enabled for user
Administrator revokes user refresh tokens
High risk users detected by Microsoft Entra ID Protection
